title: #57 Creativity
prompt: Some people said creativity is something a person was born with. Others thought creativity can be taught and developed. What’s your opinion? Explain.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: The essay argues that creativity is innate (born with) but acknowledges that practice also plays a role.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The essay argues that creativity is innate (born with) but acknowledges that practice also plays a role.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: The essay maintains a strong agreement with the view that natural talent is the primary source of creativity, while recognizing the value of learning.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The essay maintains a strong agreement with the view that natural talent is the primary source of creativity, while recognizing the value of learning.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: The essay argues that teaching creativity is beneficial, using art classes as an example.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The essay argues that teaching creativity is beneficial, using art classes as an example.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: The essay addresses the opposing view that creativity is purely natural, using the example of naturally talented children.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The essay addresses the opposing view that creativity is purely natural, using the example of naturally talented children.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: The essay argues that natural talent is a significant source of creativity, using early artistic skill as an example.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The essay argues that natural talent is a significant source of creativity, using early artistic skill as an example.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: The essay acknowledges that practice and education are also important for developing creative skills, using years of writing as an example.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The essay acknowledges that practice and education are also important for developing creative skills, using years of writing as an example.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: The first body paragraph argues that teaching methods can improve creativity, focusing on structured learning and practical skills.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The first body paragraph argues that teaching methods can improve creativity, focusing on structured learning and practical skills.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: The second body paragraph discusses the opposing view, suggesting that some creative skills are natural and inherent, but ultimately conceding to the teachable aspect.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The second body paragraph discusses the opposing view, suggesting that some creative skills are natural and inherent, but ultimately conceding to the teachable aspect.

modelPlan.focus: Discuss the nature of creativity and whether it is inherent or can be developed through teaching and practice.
keyArguments: Creativity is both inherent and can be developed through training and practice.
The interplay between inherent traits and environmental factors plays a crucial role in fostering creativity.
